_comment: tan-cli#887. `sdk list`'s `data` VALUES are whatever alp-sdk has
published on GitHub at the moment of the call, so -- exactly like
`doctor` (tan-cli#664) and unlike every byte golden under
`contract/envelopes/` -- this entry pins the `data` KEY SET and never a
value. `contract/README.md` listed `data.releases` as NOT COVERED from
the day the row was written; that is what this file closes.
Why it needed closing, given the keys were already right: measured on
the pinned v0.6.0-rc1 (`git show v0.6.0-rc1:python/tan/commands/
sdk_cmd.py`), `parse_remote_sdk_releases` ALREADY carried `draft` and
`prerelease` per entry, and has since `tan sdk` was first added
(f808e8f). tan-cli#887 was filed believing the envelope dropped them.
It did not -- but nothing pinned them either, so a rename would have
been silent on both sides, and a consumer reading `contract/README.md`
was told in as many words that the field was uncovered. Publishing the
key set turns 'happens to be emitted' into 'promised'.
Every value under `dataKeys` is a MACHINE TOKEN -- `"string"`,
`"bool"` -- never a prose sentence, same rule as
`contract/doctor-data-keys.json`. `releases` uses that file's
META-DESCRIPTOR notation (`requiredKeys`, describing the shape of each
ARRAY ELEMENT, never a field literally called `requiredKeys`); there is
no `optionalKeys` because `parse_remote_sdk_releases` builds every entry
from one dict literal, so all seven keys are unconditional.
Two defaults are part of the promise, not incidental: an entry whose
GitHub payload omits `draft`/`prerelease` (or carries a non-boolean
there) still emits both keys, as `false` -- `item.get(...) is True`,
tan-cli#122 -- and a missing string field emits `""`, never `null`
(`_str_field`). So a consumer never has to distinguish absent from
false, and `releases[].prerelease` is always a real boolean.
`releases` is `[]`, never absent, on the two paths that emit this shape
without a fetch: a bare `sdk list` with no `--online` (tan-cli#351,
exit 0) and the fetch-failure refusal. `subcommand` is `"list"` on all
three, and the unknown-subcommand failure emits this same shape with
the offending name in `subcommand` -- see `_list_data`, whose docstring
records that the Rust built that refusal out of `ListData` too.
`args` carries `--online` because that is the invocation the key set
was enumerated against; it is NOT re-run by the release workflow (which
only re-packages this file), and the lockstep test below never dials
the network -- see its own docstring for exactly what it does and does
not prove.
Renaming or dropping a key here is the same breaking wire change
`contract/README.md`'s frozen-issue-code rule describes: bump the CLI
MAJOR/MINOR, record it in CHANGELOG.md, and open the matching
alp-sdk-vscode issue.
`python/tests/conformance/test_sdk_list_contract_key_set.py` is the
lockstep check: it derives the key set FROM this file -- never from a
constant of its own -- runs the real `sdk list --online` command with
only the socket replaced, and fails on either an emitted key nobody
declared or a declared key the command stopped emitting.
